title: Extreme-Population Pharmacology as a Natural Stress-Test for Drug Safety: The Sentinel-Case Causal-Inference (DABR/FOCUS) Framework
content: Drug-safety evaluation rests on a largely implicit structural-determinist premise: that a defined molecular design feature, such as an engineered silencing modification, secures safety across host contexts. Extreme human populations living under sustained environmental stress (for example, indigenous communities at chronic high altitude) constitute naturally occurring, high-sensitivity settings in which this premise can be probed, because a molecular design that is unremarkable in a standard-population trial may behave differently under extreme host conditions. This review articulates a framework that treats extreme populations as a natural stress-test for drug safety and that converts a single, catastrophic sentinel toxicity event into defensible causal inference without over-claiming. We synthesize three strands: the theoretical case for extreme-population pharmacology as an institutionalized observation window; the methodological status of the sentinel case as a naturally imposed, exhaustively documented experiment whose inferential weight derives from inference architecture rather than sample size; and an operational four-tier causal ladder, FOCUS (spatial necessity, temporal priority, biological plausibility, and counterfactual intervention), expressed through a DABR workflow (Data-anchored, Assumption-explicit, Boundary-declared, Reproducible). FOCUS functions as a gate rather than a verdict: a claim advances only as far as its evidence supports, and unmet tiers are declared rather than imputed. We further specify the disciplines that keep a low-n framework honest, namely explicit grading of certainty, the rule that claim strength must not exceed evidence strength, and the treatment of a declared absence of evidence as an evidentiary asset. Finally, we argue that novelty should be asserted as a bounded claim, that reproducibility is a governance requirement rather than an aspiration, and that the framework's value lies in stating both the standard such studies should meet and the claims they should not make. This review is framework-level and deliberately contains no primary data claims; the applied analytic operations implied by the framework belong to companion work.
